desc: Loud-to-quiet or quiet-to-loud. The CONTRAST is the whole effect. WIRED FOR SHORTS since 2026-08-19: scripts/short.py reads audio_drop off this card and sound_dept.drop_curve dips the score across the boundary. NOT wired for .movie films - epic.py has its own audio path and does not use sound_dept.mix_master, so a smash there is still a plain cut and `silence: true` remains the workaround.
verdict: RENDERED 2026-08-04 between two real clips. THE PICTURE IS IDENTICAL TO A HARD CUT - MAD against cut exactly 0.00. Correct: the effect is the audio_drop of 0.4, and the card is explicit that the contrast is the whole point. Nothing happens to the image.
renders_in: scripts/short.py (audio only; the picture is a hard cut by design)
picture_note: Identical to a hard cut, which is CORRECT - the effect was always meant to be the audio dip, and in the shorts path that dip now exists.
broken: Half closed. audio_drop 0.4 now has a consumer in the SHORTS path (scripts/short.py -> sound_dept.drop_curve: dips to 40% of level from 0.10s before the boundary, holds 0.55s, recovers over 0.35s). It still has none in scripts/epic.py, which is the .movie renderer. Grepped 2026-08-19.
workaround: For .movie films only: put `silence: true` on the quiet side of the boundary - compile.py drops the cue for that scene and restarts it after, which buys the same contrast. Shorts need nothing; the field is honoured directly.

evidence.method: wired into scripts/short.py and sound_dept.drop_curve; the gain curve walked at nine timestamps before rendering
evidence.note: Dips to x0.40 from 0.10s before the cut, holds 0.55s, recovers over 0.35s. Deliberately shallower and shorter than a hit's breath (x0.16 for 0.35s then a slam) - a smash is punctuation, a hit is the film's moment, and matching shapes would stop the hit reading as special. Shorts only; epic.py still has no reader.
